description: Exact RGBs in M2's final 14-color quantized palette eligible for palette-variant remapping. Only the tunic (top) and trousers families are listed — skin and hair are never remapped, matching the roster-integration structural decision (#2) and beingPalette.ts's existing remap-table shape (garment-only exact-RGB swap).

tunic.note: Dominant slate-blue tunic fill (verified via a strap-clear sample rectangle).
Fold/shadow tone under the arms and strap.

trousers.note: Dominant trousers fill (verified via a boot-clear sample rectangle).

excludedFromRemap.note: M2's 14-color palette has NO cross-role color sharing between the tunic/trousers families and skin/hair/boots-and-strap (verified by a whole-file color-frequency audit across front/back/side/walk/pose frames, not just the ASCII legend — every RGB value maps to exactly one role). This is simpler than F1's case where several tones doubled up across roles. (36,16,5), the eyebrow/pupil-dark tone, is reused by touchup_m2.py as a hand-authored smile-crease on the FACE only — that is a touch-up decision, not a palette-source one, and does not put it in the tunic/trousers families.

suggestedVariant.name: moss
suggestedVariant.note: One example remap into the world's muted garment families (BEING_PALETTE_VARIANTS in beingPalette.ts: slate-blue / violet-grey / moss / ochre / bone). M2 ships in slate-blue already, so 'moss' is proposed as a visually distinct first-pass alternative for variant testing — re-validate visually against the actual atlas render before locking in for R3.
